correctness.rationale: For source X on the unit sphere inside r-plane U with second moment P_U/r, every coupling to spherical-tight Y satisfies E||X−Y||²=2−2 E<X,P_UY> >=2−2sqrt(r/d) by Hilbert-space Cauchy–Schwarz, using E||X||²=1 and E||P_U Y||²=r/d. For r<d, choose independent centered spherical tight Z in U-perp, set Y=sqrt(r/d)X+sqrt((d−r)/d)Z; then ||Y||=1 pointwise, EYY^T=I/d (including mixed terms), and cost exactly the lower bound. Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz forces P_UY=sqrt(r/d)X a.s.; its orthogonal component has constant norm and target tightness iff EZZ^T=P_Uperp/(d−r) and EXZ^T=0. Edge cases r=d cost zero and r=1 allow arbitrarily biased antipodal source; no mean-zero assumption. Entire argument analytic, not a finite experiment.
